title: soothfast baseline
description: A saved measurement run, stored as .soothfast/baselines/NAME.json. `gate`, `docs check`, `report` and `trend` read it. Readers ignore unknown keys at every level and treat a missing key as absent, so every key is optional; a baseline without `items` simply measures nothing.

version.description: Format version. Written as 1; readers ignore it.

created_unix.description: Unix seconds when the baseline was last saved.

noise_pct.description: Measured timer noise floor of the machine, in percent. Used to widen walltime gate thresholds.

build.description: What the measured binary was compiled with. Instruction counts are comparable only between equal stamps; a baseline without one reads as predating stamps.

codegen_units.description: Codegen-unit setting the gate pinned, or `inherit`.

profiles.description: Opaque hash of the cargo profile tables in effect.

rustflags.description: Opaque hash of the rustc flags from the environment and cargo config.

items.description: Measured items keyed by item id (`package::module::function`, with `-` in the package normalized to `_`; buildcost pseudo-items are `buildcost::...`).

assertions.description: Verdicts of the runner's checked claims (alloc, p99, complexity), written alongside items so reports can show verified claims.

id.description: Id of the item the assertion belongs to.

kind.description: Which claim was checked, for example `alloc`, `p99` or `complexity`.

unmeasured.description: Items the measured bench binaries contain whose numbers, or some of whose metrics, this baseline does not hold, one entry per package and reason. `docs check` reports an unchanged claim on one of them as not evaluated; a new or edited claim still fails.

package.description: Package the items belong to, as the first segment of their ids.

reason.description: `identical-binaries`: the binaries matched the merge-base and no stored run of them held the gating counters. `reused-walltime`: the walltime came from another run of the same code. `shard-missing`: the shard owning the items saved nothing. `gate-failed`: the package's gate failed or errored. `no-parent`: a push whose commit has no parent to gate against. `no-measurement`: no leg wrote anything for the package, so `items` is empty.

metrics.description: Backend names (`walltime`) or `backend.metric` the entry covers. Absent for every metric of the items.

detail.description: Human-readable reason, naming the shard or run.

items.description: Ids of the items without a measurement.

shard.description: `I/N` of the `gate --shard` run whose items this file holds. Only `baseline merge` reads it; a merged baseline has none.

listed.description: Every item id each package's bench binary lists, whichever shard owns it, keyed by package. Written beside `shard` so `baseline merge` can name the items of a shard that saved nothing.

item.description: One measured item. Each metric group is present only for the backends that ran. Unsigned integers are non-negative JSON integers; a float such as 3.0 does not read as one.

fingerprint.description: Hex FNV-1a fingerprint of the annotated item's token stream. Compared across builds to detect a changed benchmark.

covers.description: Path of the public item the benchmark covers, from `covers = ...`; empty when unset.

imported.description: Import prefix the item came from, written by `cargo soothfast import`. Absent for measured items.

tolerance_pct.description: Per-item gate threshold override, in percent.

rounds.description: Per-round medians in nanoseconds when the side ran interleaved rounds. Omitted otherwise.

ir.description: Instructions executed (Ir) per iteration. Unsigned integer.

window.description: Iterations `ir` averages over. Unsigned integer; absent when the harness did not say.

build_ms.description: Build time in milliseconds. Unsigned integer.

size_bytes.description: Artifact size in bytes. Unsigned integer.

reused.description: Set when the metrics came from a stored measurement rather than this run.

from.description: What supplied them, for example `item cache`.
